chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Abdullah ibn Aqil ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said:

Two men differed regarding a case of Ali (peace be upon him) and Umar regarding a woman whose husband had divorced her with one or two divorces, then she married another man who either divorced her or died leaving her, and when her waiting period ended, the first husband married her. Umar said: 'She remains upon whatever remains of the divorce,' while the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah, does one divorce not annul three [divorces] and not annul one?'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Umar and Ali's rulings on the validity of the first divorce after a woman marries another man and then returns to the first?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights a classic jurisprudential divergence between Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) regarding the 'annulment of divorce' (hadiym al-talaq) upon a woman's marriage to a second husband. While Umar maintained that the first husband's initial divorce remained counted, Ali argued that the intervening marriage and its subsequent dissolution effectively erased the first divorce, leaving only one count remaining for the first husband. This narration is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence to support the view that the second marriage serves as a complete reset of the divorce tally, emphasizing Ali's precise understanding of the Quranic mechanics of talaq.
